clues: This town sits in a broad valley in the mountain west of the United States. High peaks rise to the southeast, and a small creek cuts the valley floor.
Snow has been seen here in every month of the year but one, high summer. Yet it falls light, and long dry spells pass with no snow at all.
This gold town was made the territory capital in 1875. Years later, voters picked it twice, in 1892 and 1894, to keep the seat.
In 1864, four gold seekers found gold in a gulch they named Last Chance. That one strike turned a rough mining camp into a rich town fast.
The governor of Montana works in this city, in the seat of state rule. State lawmakers meet here to make the state's laws.
